text:
incident-bot: ALERT: canary-monitor/prod-primary failing (rate=8 failures/min, threshold=5) — triggered at 2026-03-15T09:12:25Z

alisha: saw this. auto-page fired. looking into scope — @mike are you able to pick this up?

mike: on it. checking canary logs + grafana now. link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/monitoring/canary-overview

sophia: FYI some deploy started ~09:05 in us-west-2 but CI shows it completed. Not sure if related.

alisha: ok. quick triage — is this noisy (flapping) or real customer impact?

mike: initial read: canary error profiles are 502/timeout spikes, looks correlated with increased latency from the inference pool. but only the synthetic probe cohort A (seq len 1024) is affected.

dan: customer impact check: product telemetry shows 0.3% increase in error rates for the last 10m in region us-west-2, mostly small requests. no large customers flagged yet.

alisha: good, low customer impact. still want to reduce pager noise. will silence page for 30m while we mitigate if we have a mitigation plan. /silence incident-bot 30m — can someone run that?

ops-bot: /silence accepted. Pager suppression applied for 30 minutes. Reason: investigating noisy canary.

mike: putting a temporary tweak: increase canary probe consecutiveFailures from 3 -> 5 to avoid single-blip pages. will also raise sampleWindow from 60s->120s for the next 15m. Pushing config now:

```
canary:
  probes:
    - name: primary-synth
      interval: 30s
      consecutiveFailures: 3   # current
      sampleWindow: 60s
```

proposed temporary patch:
```
consecutiveFailures: 5
sampleWindow: 120s
```

mike: applied to staging rule and rolled to prod canary fleet (gradual). monitoring for suppression side-effects.

alisha: thanks. mike do you see any backend throttling or an overloaded host group?

mike: no host OOMs. Some inference instances had 2x latency increase for long-context paths — likely kernel hit due to attention mem spikes. Not hitting pod restart.

sophia: suggest we add a rolling-median smoothing to the canary metric before thresholding. That should kill single-sample spikes. I can submit a PR to the canary service.

alisha: +1. but for the immediate window we want to avoid more pages. dan can you update the incident ticket with customer impact notes and monitor flags?

dan: on it. creating INC-2026-0315-canary-noise with summary + links. adding timeline.

tess: question — should we demote this alert from P0 -> P1? It currently pages all oncall.

alisha: yeah during the next 30m suppression do we change severity? I think change to warning-level (no page) but keep dashboard alert visible. mike can you update alert policy?

mike: changing alert rule: severity: critical -> warning (no page) for this specific probe ID. Also adding tag `probe_cohort=A` so we can scope later. Pushed in alertmanager.

incident-bot: Alert rule update applied by mike at 2026-03-15T09:28:40Z.

alisha: long-term items we should decide in the postmortem:
- adjust consecutiveFailures default for synthetic probes from 3->6 for long-context probes
- increase default sample interval from 30s->60s for non-user-facing probes
- add rolling-median(3) smoothing to the canary metric pipeline
- create grafana dashboard with per-cohort failure breakdown and noise rate (alerts/hr)
- add automatic suppression during deploy windows (match deploy tag)

sophia: I'll draft the PR for smoothing and a config flag `alert_smoothing_enabled` so we can flip per-cohort.

mike: I'll open an alertmanager rule change RFC and include the metrics we will track to confirm reduced noise: alerts_per_hour, false_positive_rate_by_cohort.

dan: scheduled a follow-up post-incident review for 2026-03-15T15:00 UTC. inviting eng-oncall, eng-sre, eng-runtime.

tess: assigning action items:
- sophia -> smoothing PR + unit tests
- mike -> alert RFC + dashboard skeleton
- dan -> incident postmortem + customer impact section
- alisha -> verify deploy correlation and runbook updates

alisha: thanks team. one more check: after raising consecutiveFailures to 5 we saw alert frequency drop from ~12->2 in last 10m. Good. Keep watching for 30m.

mike: confirm metrics: alerts/hr (canary-probe) before=18, last10m=2, probe-fail-rate stable at 5-7/min for cohort A.

sophia: iterating on PR now. will add a feature flag and a small dashboard panel for smoothing effect so we can A/B.

dan: wrote note to support: "No customer-facing impact observed beyond minor error rate increase; system teams investigating. We'll update in 1h."

alisha: handoff — my shift ends in 25m. @mike you'll be primary after I go offline. mike ack?

mike: ack. I'll own until postmortem. If things re-page, escalate to eng-sre.

ops-bot: Reminder: silence expires in 25 minutes.

alisha: thanks. leaving a short runbook snippet here for oncall followup:
1) check grafana canary-overview -> cohort breakdown
2) check probe host latencies -> /logs/inference/<host>
3) if alerts spike >5/hr -> un-silence and notify eng-sre
4) if customer errors >1% -> invoke incident escalation

mike: noted. I'll also run a quick sweep to see if any other cohorts (B/C) are starting to show early signs.

tess: appreciate the quick fix and the plan. We'll review rate thresholds and smoothing in the postmortem.

alisha: signing off now — thanks everyone.

mike: good work. I'll post follow-up when the postmortem doc is ready (link in thread).
